summary: Ephemeral API key window skew causing repeat 429s for multipart uploader workers
description:
Issue summary:
Skylark Media reports repeated 429 responses from the uploads/part/complete endpoint during high-concurrency multipart uploads. The customer uses ephemeral API keys generated per-upload-worker (short TTL ~ 90s) and a pool of 64 concurrent workers. The 429s began after they moved large backfills from staging to their dedicated pool in us-east.

Impact:
Several upload jobs fail mid-flight, triggering retries and increasing cost. Customer reports ~18% of upload parts receive 429s under a sustained 800 rps fanout. Business impact is elevated because the upload pipeline feeds user-facing content ingestion.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: skylark-dedicated-us-east
- Region: us-east-1
- API surface: REST multipart upload endpoints (uploads/init, uploads/part, uploads/part/complete)
- Keys: ephemeral per-worker API keys with TTL ~90s issued by Skylark's orchestration

Observed behaviour:
- 429s concentrated on uploads/part/complete and occasionally uploads/part when many short-lived keys are created and destroyed rapidly.
- Token bucket headers show client-facing X-RateLimit-* varying by key; aggregated tenant token usage remains within tenant quota in the console.
- Edge logs show different window_starts for keys created within 5–10s of each other.
- Healthcheck/keepalive traffic not implicated.

Expected behaviour:
- Short-lived keys should inherit clean accounting into per-key windows without causing tenant-level bursts that lead to server-side 429s for the same tenant.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
steps_to_reproduce: Generate ephemeral API keys with TTL=90s and distribute to 64 parallel upload workers.
Kick off multipart uploads with 100 concurrent files, each with 8 parts, so part-complete calls interleave across keys.
Observe error rate on uploads/part/complete and token bucket headers returned in responses.
Repeat with keys that have longer TTL (10m) to confirm drop in 429 rate.
logs:
Representative log lines (edge):
[2026-03-08T14:02:10Z] key=ephemeral-xx window_start=2026-03-08T14:01:30Z token_count=1 increment=1 -> ALLOW
[2026-03-08T14:02:11Z] key=ephemeral-yy window_start=2026-03-08T14:02:00Z token_count=1 increment=1 -> ALLOW
[2026-03-08T14:02:11Z] tenant=skylark tenant_count=780 increment=64 -> ALLOW
[2026-03-08T14:02:12Z] key=ephemeral-zz window_start=2026-03-08T14:01:30Z token_count=0 increment=1 -> THROTTLE (429)

Note: timestamps show window_start misalignment between concurrently minted ephemeral keys.
investigation_notes:
Support repro attempt: We reproduced locally by issuing short TTL keys from the token service and driving parallel part-complete calls. Observed increased 429s when key creation events clustered such that window_start values for keys fell into different bucket boundaries.

Hypothesis 1: Window alignment skew across the edge-proxy cluster causes per-key windows to be short/fragmented immediately after issuance; short-lived keys get charged into multiple windows during warmup, exhausting per-key or per-route micro-windows faster.
Hypothesis 2: Edge token accounting path applies a small fixed reservation on key creation that double-counts when keys are reissued rapidly by orchestration; this appears only under our dedicated pool configuration where edge-proxy version 1.8.2 is routed.

Quick checks performed:
- Verified tenant-level quota shows no exhaustion during the event window (console metrics).
- Compared behavior with long-lived keys (10m TTL) — 429s drop to <1%.
- Confirmed edge-proxy processes were a mix of 1.8.1 and 1.8.2 during the customer's incident window.
- Reviewed related past tickets about key rotation (linked SUP-76121) and healthcheck counts (linked SUP-427801) for patterns.
proposed_next_steps:
1) Temporarily advise customer to increase TTL to >10m for upload workers as a mitigation.
2) Rotate edge-proxy fleet to homogeneous 1.8.2+ with the patch from PR 889 to stabilize window alignment.
3) Add telemetry to rate-limiter to emit window_start skew histogram per-key for short-lived keys.
4) Engineering to review token reservation logic on key issuance; add unit test that simulates high churn of ephemeral keys.

We have already opened an internal PR (see related_github_prs) to add additional logging; SRE will schedule a controlled repro on dedicated pool next week.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: customer temporarily increased ephemeral key TTL to 15 minutes which immediately reduced 429s to baseline. Edge fleet rotation completed to v1.8.3 with fix from PR 889; subsequent repro with short TTL keys showed markedly lower 429s and aligned window_start headers.

Permanent fix: Engineering patch removed double-reservation in token issue path and added skew-tolerant windowing for per-key accounting. Patch rolled to dedicated pools during a low-traffic maintenance window. Follow-up: add a console advisory for recommended TTLs for ephemeral keys used by high-concurrency upload workers.

Status: Resolved for customer; monitoring for 72h post-deploy.
